This is a narrative-style transcript without explicit speaker markers. The
chunker should fall back to paragraph-based splitting when it doesn't see
two or more speaker-prefixed turns at the start of the text.

We were deciding between FastAPI and Flask for the backend. Flask is
older and more familiar, but FastAPI's Pydantic integration is cleaner
for this kind of schema-heavy project, and the auto-generated OpenAPI
docs make the local token-auth endpoint easier to test from a curl one-
liner. The call was to go with FastAPI.

We also discussed the choice between a Manifest V2 vs V3 extension. V2
is deprecated and will stop working in current Chrome versions, so V3 is
the only sane path. The service worker constraints are annoying but
workable: the auth token lives in chrome.storage.local and is read by
the service worker once on extension load.

For the dedup threshold, 0.7 was picked as a starting guess and flagged
as needing real-world tuning. The blueprint is explicit that this number
is not validated.

For the brief length, the hard constraint is 300 words. Truncate rather
than overflow. The user has been firm on this — silently returning a
longer brief would be a bug.
